title: Rate-limited API proxy at the edge
description: Use Workers KV and Durable Objects to throttle requests before they reach your origin.
overview: A Cloudflare Worker that rate-limits incoming API requests per client using a Durable Object for strict, race-free enforcement on hot endpoints, with Workers KV available for longer-lived counters.
prerequisites: A Cloudflare account with Workers enabled
A KV namespace and Durable Object binding configured in wrangler.toml

steps.title: Create the Worker project
steps.content: Scaffold a new Worker with Wrangler.

code.code:
npm create cloudflare@latest rate-limit-proxy
cd rate-limit-proxy

steps.title: Define the Durable Object
steps.content: Each client gets its own Durable Object instance that tracks a sliding window of request timestamps in memory.

steps.title: Route requests through the limiter
steps.content: In the main Worker, derive a Durable Object ID from the client's IP or API key, then forward the check before proxying to the origin.

steps.title: Bind the Durable Object
steps.content: Declare the class and a KV namespace for longer-lived counters in wrangler.toml.

steps.title: Deploy and test
steps.content: Publish the Worker and send requests past the threshold to confirm it returns a 429 once the limit is hit.

architecture: Each client is mapped to a single Durable Object instance by IP or API key, giving strictly consistent, race-free counting even under concurrent requests at the edge, something KV alone can't guarantee due to eventual consistency. The Worker checks the limiter before proxying to origin, so blocked requests never leave Cloudflare's network.
result: An edge-deployed proxy that enforces a 60-requests-per-minute limit per client with sub-millisecond overhead, protecting the origin from abuse without adding a centralized rate-limiting service.

troubleshooting.cause: CF-Connecting-IP is missing in local testing, so all requests share the same empty-string Durable Object ID.
troubleshooting.fix: Test through a real Cloudflare-proxied request, or key the Durable Object off a header you control locally instead.

troubleshooting.issue: wrangler deploy fails with 'Durable Object migration required'
troubleshooting.cause: New Durable Object classes need an explicit migration entry in wrangler.toml before Cloudflare will provision them.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a [[migrations]] block with a tag and new_classes listing RateLimiter.

troubleshooting.issue: Rate limits reset unexpectedly right after a deploy
troubleshooting.cause: Durable Object instances can be recreated on deploy, which clears their in-memory request array.
troubleshooting.fix: Persist counters to the Durable Object's storage API instead of relying only on the in-memory array.

nextSteps: Persist request counts to Durable Object storage so limits survive restarts.
Add a response header showing remaining quota to help API consumers.
Make the limit and window configurable via environment variables.
